sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16,071.7 million, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9 million [F6][F7][D241][D292].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth on $5,828.0 million of US sales, and US net product sales grew 117.6% [S48][D582][D470].
REGEN-COV fell to zero in FY2022 and US net product sales dropped 43.1% [S49][D473].
Since then growth has slowed to 5.6% a year over FY2022..FY2025, with FY2025 up only 1.0% [D767][D440].
The growth engine has rotated from EYLEA to collaboration profit shares: EYLEA US was 63.0% of revenue in FY2017 but 19.2% in FY2025 [D554][D576].
EYLEA US sales fell 42.4% in FY2025 to $2,747.8 million on lower volumes and a lower net selling price amid competitive pressure and the EYLEA HD transition [S43][D577][P10].
EYLEA HD partly offset that, rising 36.3% to $1,636.9 million on higher volumes [S64][D613][P11].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits contributed 9.3pp of FY2025 growth and reached 36.5% of revenue [D592][D590].
That share rose 33.6% to $5,241.6 million, driven by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][P9].
Operating income fell 10.3% in FY2025 while revenue rose 1.0%, so there was no operating leverage [F20][D441][D440].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][F26][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the FY2025 margin as it rose 14.0% to $5,850.2 million, or 40.8% of revenue [D465][X34][D455][D420].
SG&A added 2.0pp back, falling 8.6% to $2,700.0 million, which the filing attributes to lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D466][X47][D456][P5].
Below the line, other income of $1,652.8 million lifted net margin to 31.4%, 6.5pp above operating margin [X117][F50][D797].
The effective tax rate rose to 13.9% from 7.7%, partly on a $44.5 million OBBBA deferred-tax charge [D427][D378][P3].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income in FY2025, in line with the 1.10x window median [F80][F40][D428][D787].
Free cash flow of $4,080.5 million was 0.91x net income and a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% median [F100][D429][D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898.4 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [F90][D447][D424][D430].
The FY2021 receivables build from REGEN-COV sales to the US government explains the swing in conversion that year [P39].
Net cash reached $16,879.9 million, 117.7% of revenue, against a peer median of -50.7% (n=8) [D434][D435][D781].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of the peer group, with debt flat at $1,985.9 million [D780][F187].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3,808.9 million consumed 93.3% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D436][D437][D459].
FY2025 included a first dividend of $370.3 million alongside $3,438.6 million of repurchases [X140][X137].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The decline reflects a mix shift toward lower-margin collaboration profit shares and heavy R&D, not a one-off [D590][D420].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table is a later recast ($5,145.6 million and $6,557.6 million) versus $6,710.8 million and $7,863.4 million as first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 decline and FY2019 rebound should not be read at face value [R2].
Watch whether operating margin holds above the FY2025 low of 24.9%; a further decline would extend the four-year slide [F30][D749][R1].
Watch EYLEA US sales against the FY2025 level of $2,747.8 million; stabilization would break the 42.4% decline [S43][D577].
Watch R&D as a share of revenue against the 40.8% FY2025 level and 34.6% median; a move back toward the median would restore leverage [D420][D760].
